To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the construction of a protease‐deficiency host of B. subti lis for the secretion of foreign protein can be achieved by inactivating the proteases that are unfavorable for the secretion of the foreign protein.

a novel evaluation system for identifying the favorable and unfavorable extracellular proteases for a foreign protein was developed and applied to construct a protease‐deficiency host of B. subilis for secretion of a target protein.
a novel evaluation system for protease‐deficiency in Bacillus subtilisis established and the system was successfully used for the secretion of foreign protein in B.subtilis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of a protease‐deficiency strain of B. sub tilis and its use in protein secretion.
the construction of a second generation protease deficient B. subtili s for secretion of foreign protein.
the construction of a personalized protease deficient host for the expression of a foreign protein and the optimization of its production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the favorable proteases are protease A (prtA), protease B (prtB), and protease Y (pry).
the protease‐deficiency strategy can be used to improve the production of a foreign protein by tailoring an appropriate protease‐defective strain.
the favorable protease for the secretion of a target protein is not necessarily one of the eight proteases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proteases of B. subti lis are not always harmful for the secretion of a target protein, and the protease‐deficiency should be tailored to meet the requirement of a specific foreign protein.

the proteases of B. subtiilis are classified into favorable and unfavorable ones, and the unfavorable proteases should be inactivated to construct a personalized protease ‐deficient host for the optimal secretion of a target protein.

the favorable and unfavorable effects of each of the eight extracellular protease on the secretion of a target protein could be identified by comparing the production level of the target protein in the mutant strains with the protease‐deficiency mutant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we developed a new strategy to improve the secretion of foreign protein in Bacillus subtili s by constructing protease‐defective strains and selecting the optimal one.
a protease‐defi cient host can be constructed for the secretion of foreign protein in B.subtilis through inactivating unfavorable proteases and retaining favorable proteases.
we have developed a strategy to construct a personalized protease deficient host for the expression of foreign proteins in B. subtiilis.
